[112](https://docs.rs#112)enum State {
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    /// Nothing interesting is going on.
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    None,
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// We have a value left over from --option=value.
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    PendingValue(OsString),
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    /// We're in the middle of -abc.
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    ///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// On Windows and other non-UTF8-OsString platforms this Vec should
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    /// only ever contain valid UTF-8 (and could instead be a String).
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    Shorts(Vec<u8>, usize),
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    #[cfg(windows)]
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// We're in the middle of -ab� on Windows (invalid UTF-16).
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    ShortsU16(Vec<u16>, usize),
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    /// We saw -- and know no more options are coming.
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    FinishedOpts,
[127](https://docs.rs#127)}
[128](https://docs.rs#128)
[129](https://docs.rs#129)/// We use this to keep track of the last emitted option, for error messages when
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// an expected value is not found.
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// We also use this as storage for long options so we can hand out &str
[133](https://docs.rs#133)/// (because String doesn't support pattern matching).
[134](https://docs.rs#134)#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[135](https://docs.rs#135)enum LastOption {
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    None,
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    Short(char),
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    Long(String),
[139](https://docs.rs#139)}

[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// A command line argument found by [`Parser`], either an option or a positional argument.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
[143](https://docs.rs#143)pub enum Arg<'a> {
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    /// A short option, e.g. `Short('q')` for `-q`.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    Short(char),
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    /// A long option, e.g. `Long("verbose")` for `--verbose`. (The dashes are not included.)
[147](https://docs.rs#147)    Long(&'a str),
[148](https://docs.rs#148)    /// A positional argument, e.g. `/dev/null`.
[149](https://docs.rs#149)    Value(OsString),
[150](https://docs.rs#150)}
[151](https://docs.rs#151)
[152](https://docs.rs#152)impl Parser {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)    /// Get the next option or positional argument.
[154](https://docs.rs#154)    ///
[155](https://docs.rs#155)    /// A return value of `Ok(None)` means the command line has been exhausted.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)    ///
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    /// Options that are not valid unicode are transformed with replacement
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// characters as by [`String::from_utf8_lossy`].
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    ///
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    /// # Errors
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    ///
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    /// [`Error::UnexpectedValue`] is returned if the last option had a
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    /// value that hasn't been consumed, as in `--option=value` or `-o=value`.
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    ///
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    /// It's possible to continue parsing after an error (but this is rarely useful).
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Arg<'_>>, Error> {
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        match self.state {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)            State::PendingValue(ref mut value) => {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)                // Last time we got `--long=value`, and `value` hasn't been used.
[170](https://docs.rs#170)                let value = replace(value, OsString::new());
[171](https://docs.rs#171)                self.state = State::None;
[172](https://docs.rs#172)                return Err(Error::UnexpectedValue {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)                    option: self
[174](https://docs.rs#174)                        .format_last_option()
[175](https://docs.rs#175)                        .expect("Should only have pending value after long option"),
[176](https://docs.rs#176)                    value,
[177](https://docs.rs#177)                });
[178](https://docs.rs#178)            }
[179](https://docs.rs#179)            State::Shorts(ref arg, ref mut pos) => {
[180](https://docs.rs#180)                // We're somewhere inside a -abc chain. Because we're in .next(),
[181](https://docs.rs#181)                // not .value(), we can assume that the next character is another option.
[182](https://docs.rs#182)                match first_codepoint(&arg[*pos..]) {
[183](https://docs.rs#183)                    Ok(None) => {
[184](https://docs.rs#184)                        self.state = State::None;
[185](https://docs.rs#185)                    }
[186](https://docs.rs#186)                    // If we find "-=[...]" we interpret it as an option.
[187](https://docs.rs#187)                    // If we find "-o=..." then there's an unexpected value.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)                    // ('-=' as an option exists, see https://linux.die.net/man/1/a2ps.
[189](https://docs.rs#189)                    // Though if you have one you should maybe disable short_equals.)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)                    // clap always interprets it as a short flag in this case, but
[191](https://docs.rs#191)                    // that feels sloppy.
[192](https://docs.rs#192)                    Ok(Some('=')) if *pos > 1 && self.short_equals => {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)                        return Err(Error::UnexpectedValue {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)                            option: self.format_last_option().unwrap(),
[195](https://docs.rs#195)                            value: self.optional_value().unwrap(),
[196](https://docs.rs#196)                        });
[197](https://docs.rs#197)                    }
[198](https://docs.rs#198)                    Ok(Some(ch)) => {
[199](https://docs.rs#199)                        *pos += ch.len_utf8();
[200](https://docs.rs#200)                        self.last_option = LastOption::Short(ch);
[201](https://docs.rs#201)                        return Ok(Some(Arg::Short(ch)));
[202](https://docs.rs#202)                    }
[203](https://docs.rs#203)                    Err(err) => {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)                        // Advancing may allow recovery.
[205](https://docs.rs#205)                        // This is a little iffy, there might be more bad unicode next.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)                        match err.error_len() {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)                            Some(len) => *pos += len,
[208](https://docs.rs#208)                            None => *pos = arg.len(),
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                        }
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                        self.last_option = LastOption::Short('�');
[211](https://docs.rs#211)                        return Ok(Some(Arg::Short('�')));
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                    }
[213](https://docs.rs#213)                }
[214](https://docs.rs#214)            }
[215](https://docs.rs#215)            #[cfg(windows)]
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            State::ShortsU16(ref arg, ref mut pos) => match first_utf16_codepoint(&arg[*pos..]) {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)                Ok(None) => {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)                    self.state = State::None;
[219](https://docs.rs#219)                }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)                Ok(Some('=')) if *pos > 1 && self.short_equals => {
[221](https://docs.rs#221)                    return Err(Error::UnexpectedValue {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)                        option: self.format_last_option().unwrap(),
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                        value: self.optional_value().unwrap(),
[224](https://docs.rs#224)                    });
[225](https://docs.rs#225)                }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                Ok(Some(ch)) => {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)                    *pos += ch.len_utf16();
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                    self.last_option = LastOption::Short(ch);
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                    return Ok(Some(Arg::Short(ch)));
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)                Err(_) => {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)                    *pos += 1;
[233](https://docs.rs#233)                    self.last_option = LastOption::Short('�');
[234](https://docs.rs#234)                    return Ok(Some(Arg::Short('�')));
[235](https://docs.rs#235)                }
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            },
[237](https://docs.rs#237)            State::FinishedOpts => {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                return Ok(self.source.next().map(Arg::Value));
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            }
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            State::None => (),
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        }
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        match self.state {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)            State::None => (),
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            ref state => panic!("unexpected state {:?}", state),
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        }
[247](https://docs.rs#247)
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        let arg = match self.source.next() {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            Some(arg) => arg,
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            None => return Ok(None),
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        };
[252](https://docs.rs#252)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)        if arg == "--" {
[254](https://docs.rs#254)            self.state = State::FinishedOpts;
[255](https://docs.rs#255)            return self.next();
[256](https://docs.rs#256)        }
[257](https://docs.rs#257)
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        #[cfg(unix)]
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        {
[260](https://docs.rs#260)            // Fast solution for platforms where OsStrings are just UTF-8-ish bytes
[261](https://docs.rs#261)            let mut arg = arg.into_vec();
[262](https://docs.rs#262)            if arg.starts_with(b"--") {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                // Long options have two forms: --option and --option=value.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                if let Some(ind) = arg.iter().position(|&b| b == b'=') {
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                    // The value can be an OsString...
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                    self.state = State::PendingValue(OsString::from_vec(arg[ind + 1..].into()));
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                    arg.truncate(ind);
[268](https://docs.rs#268)                }
[269](https://docs.rs#269)                // ...but the option has to be a string.
[270](https://docs.rs#270)                // String::from_utf8_lossy().into_owned() would work, but its
[271](https://docs.rs#271)                // return type is Cow: if the original was valid a borrowed
[272](https://docs.rs#272)                // version is returned, and then into_owned() does an
[273](https://docs.rs#273)                // unnecessary copy.
[274](https://docs.rs#274)                // By trying String::from_utf8 first we avoid that copy if arg
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                // is already UTF-8 (which is most of the time).
[276](https://docs.rs#276)                // reqwest does a similar maneuver more efficiently with unsafe:
[277](https://docs.rs#277)                // https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/e6a1a09f0904e06de4ff1317278798c4ed28af66/src/async_impl/response.rs#L194
[278](https://docs.rs#278)                let option = match String::from_utf8(arg) {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                    Ok(text) => text,
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                    Err(err) => String::from_utf8_lossy(err.as_bytes()).into_owned(),
[281](https://docs.rs#281)                };
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                Ok(Some(self.set_long(option)))
[283](https://docs.rs#283)            } else if arg.len() > 1 && arg[0] == b'-' {
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                self.state = State::Shorts(arg, 1);
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                self.next()
[286](https://docs.rs#286)            } else {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                Ok(Some(Arg::Value(OsString::from_vec(arg))))
[288](https://docs.rs#288)            }
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        #[cfg(not(unix))]
[292](https://docs.rs#292)        {
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            // Platforms where looking inside an OsString is harder
[294](https://docs.rs#294)
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            #[cfg(windows)]
[296](https://docs.rs#296)            {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)                // Fast path for Windows
[298](https://docs.rs#298)                let mut bytes = arg.encode_wide();
[299](https://docs.rs#299)                const DASH: u16 = b'-' as u16;
[300](https://docs.rs#300)                match (bytes.next(), bytes.next()) {
[301](https://docs.rs#301)                    (Some(DASH), Some(_)) => {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)                        // This is an option, we'll have to do more work.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)                        // (We already checked for "--" earlier.)
[304](https://docs.rs#304)                    }
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                    _ => {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                        // Just a value, return early.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                        return Ok(Some(Arg::Value(arg)));
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                    }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                }
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            }
[311](https://docs.rs#311)
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            let mut arg = match arg.into_string() {
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                Ok(arg) => arg,
[314](https://docs.rs#314)                Err(arg) => {
[315](https://docs.rs#315)                    // The argument is not valid unicode.
[316](https://docs.rs#316)                    // If it's an option we'll have to do something nasty,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                    // otherwise we can return it as-is.
[318](https://docs.rs#318)
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                    #[cfg(windows)]
[320](https://docs.rs#320)                    {
[321](https://docs.rs#321)                        // On Windows we can only get here if this is an option, otherwise
[322](https://docs.rs#322)                        // we return earlier.
[323](https://docs.rs#323)                        // Unlike on Unix, we can't efficiently process invalid unicode.
[324](https://docs.rs#324)                        // Semantically it's UTF-16, but internally it's WTF-8 (a superset of UTF-8).
[325](https://docs.rs#325)                        // So we only process the raw version here, when we know we really have to.
[326](https://docs.rs#326)                        let mut arg: Vec<u16> = arg.encode_wide().collect();
[327](https://docs.rs#327)                        const DASH: u16 = b'-' as u16;
[328](https://docs.rs#328)                        const EQ: u16 = b'=' as u16;
[329](https://docs.rs#329)                        if arg.starts_with(&[DASH, DASH]) {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)                            if let Some(ind) = arg.iter().position(|&u| u == EQ) {
[331](https://docs.rs#331)                                self.state =
[332](https://docs.rs#332)                                    State::PendingValue(OsString::from_wide(&arg[ind + 1..]));
[333](https://docs.rs#333)                                arg.truncate(ind);
[334](https://docs.rs#334)                            }
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                            let long = self.set_long(String::from_utf16_lossy(&arg));
[336](https://docs.rs#336)                            return Ok(Some(long));
[337](https://docs.rs#337)                        } else {
[338](https://docs.rs#338)                            assert!(arg.len() > 1);
[339](https://docs.rs#339)                            assert_eq!(arg[0], DASH);
[340](https://docs.rs#340)                            self.state = State::ShortsU16(arg, 1);
[341](https://docs.rs#341)                            return self.next();
[342](https://docs.rs#342)                        }
[343](https://docs.rs#343)                    };
[344](https://docs.rs#344)
[345](https://docs.rs#345)                    #[cfg(not(windows))]
[346](https://docs.rs#346)                    {
[347](https://docs.rs#347)                        // Other platforms.
[348](https://docs.rs#348)
[349](https://docs.rs#349)                        // Most of them have their own `OsStrExt` but that doesn't mean
[350](https://docs.rs#350)                        // they actually have invalid strings. WASI for example exports
[351](https://docs.rs#351)                        // the Unix extension trait even though only UTF-8 OS strings
[352](https://docs.rs#352)                        // are allowed.
[353](https://docs.rs#353)                        // So on WASI this code path is only reachable by creating custom
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                        // faulty OS strings, not by processing true environment args.
[355](https://docs.rs#355)
[356](https://docs.rs#356)                        // This allocates unconditionally, sadly.
[357](https://docs.rs#357)                        let text = arg.to_string_lossy();
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                        if text.starts_with('-') {
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                            // Use the lossily patched version and hope for the best.
[360](https://docs.rs#360)                            // This may be incorrect behavior.
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                            // Other options are returning an error or (as of Rust 1.74)
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                            // using the unsafe encoded_bytes API. But neither seem worth
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                            // it in this obscure corner, especially since they'd be hard
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                            // to test.
[365](https://docs.rs#365)                            // (The entire crate will most likely move to the encoded_bytes
[366](https://docs.rs#366)                            // API in the future, once it supports checked conversion.)
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                            // Please open an issue if this behavior affects you!
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                            text.into_owned()
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                        } else {
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                            // It didn't look like an option, so return it as a value.
[371](https://docs.rs#371)                            return Ok(Some(Arg::Value(arg)));
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                        }
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                    }
[374](https://docs.rs#374)                }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            };
[376](https://docs.rs#376)
[377](https://docs.rs#377)            // The argument is valid unicode. This is the ideal version of the
[378](https://docs.rs#378)            // code, the previous mess was purely to deal with invalid unicode.
[379](https://docs.rs#379)            if arg.starts_with("--") {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)                if let Some(ind) = arg.find('=') {
[381](https://docs.rs#381)                    self.state = State::PendingValue(arg[ind + 1..].into());
[382](https://docs.rs#382)                    arg.truncate(ind);
[383](https://docs.rs#383)                }
[384](https://docs.rs#384)                Ok(Some(self.set_long(arg)))
[385](https://docs.rs#385)            } else if arg.starts_with('-') && arg != "-" {
[386](https://docs.rs#386)                self.state = State::Shorts(arg.into(), 1);
[387](https://docs.rs#387)                self.next()
[388](https://docs.rs#388)            } else {
[389](https://docs.rs#389)                Ok(Some(Arg::Value(arg.into())))
[390](https://docs.rs#390)            }
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        }
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    }
[393](https://docs.rs#393)
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    /// Get a value for an option.
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    ///
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// This function should normally be called right after seeing an option
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    /// that expects a value, with positional arguments being collected
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// using [`next()`][Parser::next].
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    ///
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// A value is collected even if it looks like an option
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// (i.e., starts with `-`).
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    ///
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// # Errors
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    ///
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// An [`Error::MissingValue`] is returned if the end of the command
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// line is reached.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    pub fn value(&mut self) -> Result<OsString, Error> {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        if let Some(value) = self.optional_value() {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)            return Ok(value);
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        }
[411](https://docs.rs#411)
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        if let Some(value) = self.source.next() {
[413](https://docs.rs#413)            return Ok(value);
[414](https://docs.rs#414)        }
[415](https://docs.rs#415)
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        Err(Error::MissingValue {
[417](https://docs.rs#417)            option: self.format_last_option(),
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        })
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    }
[420](https://docs.rs#420)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    /// Gather multiple values for an option.
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    ///
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// This is used for options that take multiple arguments, such as a
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// `--command` flag that's invoked as `app --command echo 'Hello world'`.
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    ///
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// It will gather arguments until another option is found, or `--` is found, or
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// the end of the command line is reached. This differs from `.value()`, which
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    /// takes a value even if it looks like an option.
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    ///
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// On success the resulting iterator will yield at least one value.
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    ///
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// An equals sign (`=`) will limit this to a single value. That means `-a=b c` and
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// `--opt=b c` will only yield `"b"` while `-a b c`, `-ab c` and `--opt b c` will
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// yield `"b"`, `"c"`.
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    ///
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    /// (If [`short_equals`](Self::set_short_equals) is disabled then `-a=b c` will yield
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// `"=b"`, `"c"`.)
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    ///
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    /// # Errors
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// If not at least one value is found then [`Error::MissingValue`] is returned.
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    ///
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    /// # Example
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    /// ```
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// # fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    /// # use lexopt::prelude::*;
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    /// # use std::ffi::OsString;
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    /// # let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_args(&["a", "b", "-x", "one", "two", "three", "four"]);
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    /// let arguments: Vec<OsString> = parser.values()?.collect();
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    /// # assert_eq!(arguments, &["a", "b"]);
[451](https://docs.rs#451)    /// # let _ = parser.next();
[452](https://docs.rs#452)    /// let at_most_three_files: Vec<PathBuf> = parser.values()?.take(3).map(Into::into).collect();
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    /// # assert_eq!(parser.raw_args()?.as_slice(), &["four"]);
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    /// for value in parser.values()? {
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    ///     // ...
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    /// }
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    /// # Ok(()) }
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    /// ```
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    pub fn values(&mut self) -> Result<ValuesIter<'_>, Error> {
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        // This code is designed so that just calling .values() doesn't consume
[461](https://docs.rs#461)        // any arguments as long as you don't use the iterator. It used to work
[462](https://docs.rs#462)        // differently.
[463](https://docs.rs#463)        // "--" is treated like an option and not consumed. This seems to me the
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        // least unreasonable behavior, and it's the easiest to implement.
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        if self.has_pending() || self.next_is_normal() {
[466](https://docs.rs#466)            Ok(ValuesIter {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)                took_first: false,
[468](https://docs.rs#468)                parser: Some(self),
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            })
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        } else {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)            Err(Error::MissingValue {
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                option: self.format_last_option(),
[473](https://docs.rs#473)            })
[474](https://docs.rs#474)        }
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    }
[476](https://docs.rs#476)
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    /// Inspect an argument and consume it if it's "normal" (not an option or --).
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    ///
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    /// Used by [`Parser::values`].
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    ///
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// This method should not be called while partway through processing an
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    /// argument.
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    fn next_if_normal(&mut self) -> Option<OsString> {
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        if self.next_is_normal() {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)            self.source.next()
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        } else {
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            None
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        }
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    }
[490](https://docs.rs#490)
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    /// Execute the check for next_if_normal().
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    fn next_is_normal(&self) -> bool {
[493](https://docs.rs#493)        assert!(!self.has_pending());
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        let arg = match self.source.as_slice().first() {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            // There has to be a next argument.
[496](https://docs.rs#496)            None => return false,
[497](https://docs.rs#497)            Some(arg) => arg,
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        };
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        if let State::FinishedOpts = self.state {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)            // If we already found a -- then we're really not supposed to be here,
[501](https://docs.rs#501)            // but we shouldn't treat the next argument as an option.
[502](https://docs.rs#502)            return true;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        }
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        if arg == "-" {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)            // "-" is the one argument with a leading '-' that's allowed.
[506](https://docs.rs#506)            return true;
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        }
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        #[cfg(unix)]
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        let lead_dash = arg.as_bytes().first() == Some(&b'-');
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        #[cfg(windows)]
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        let lead_dash = arg.encode_wide().next() == Some(b'-' as u16);
[512](https://docs.rs#512)        #[cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))]
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        let lead_dash = arg.to_string_lossy().as_bytes().first() == Some(&b'-');
[514](https://docs.rs#514)
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        !lead_dash
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    /// Take raw arguments from the original command line.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    ///
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    /// This returns an iterator of [`OsString`]s. Any arguments that are not
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    /// consumed are kept, so you can continue parsing after you're done with
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    /// the iterator.
[523](https://docs.rs#523)    ///
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    /// To inspect an argument without consuming it, use [`RawArgs::peek`] or
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    /// [`RawArgs::as_slice`].
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    ///
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    /// # Errors
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    ///
[529](https://docs.rs#529)    /// Returns an [`Error::UnexpectedValue`] if the last option had a left-over
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// argument, as in `--option=value`, `-ovalue`, or if it was midway through
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    /// an option chain, as in `-abc`. The iterator only yields whole arguments.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// To avoid this, use [`try_raw_args()`][Parser::try_raw_args].
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    ///
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// After this error the method is guaranteed to succeed, as it consumes the
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    /// rest of the argument.
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    ///
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    /// # Example
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// As soon as a free-standing argument is found, consume the other arguments
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    /// as-is, and build them into a command.
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// ```
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// # fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    /// # use lexopt::prelude::*;
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// # use std::ffi::OsString;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    /// # let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_args(&["-x", "echo", "-n", "'Hello, world'"]);
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    /// # while let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    /// # match arg {
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    /// Value(prog) => {
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    ///     let args: Vec<_> = parser.raw_args()?.collect();
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    ///     let command = std::process::Command::new(prog).args(args);
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    /// }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    /// # _ => (), }} Ok(()) }
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// ```
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    pub fn raw_args(&mut self) -> Result<RawArgs<'_>, Error> {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        if let Some(value) = self.optional_value() {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            return Err(Error::UnexpectedValue {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                option: self.format_last_option().unwrap(),
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                value,
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            });
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        Ok(RawArgs(&mut self.source))
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    }
[564](https://docs.rs#564)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// Take raw arguments from the original command line, *if* the current argument
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    /// has finished processing.
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    ///
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// Unlike [`raw_args()`][Parser::raw_args] this does not consume any value
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// in case of a left-over argument. This makes it safe to call at any time.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    ///
[571](https://docs.rs#571)    /// It returns `None` exactly when [`optional_value()`][Parser::optional_value]
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    /// would return `Some`.
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    ///
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    /// Note: If no arguments are left then it returns an empty iterator (not `None`).
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    ///
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    /// # Example
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    /// Process arguments of the form `-123` as numbers. For a complete runnable version of
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    /// this example, see
[579](https://docs.rs#579)    /// [`examples/nonstandard.rs`](https://github.com/blyxxyz/lexopt/blob/e3754e6f24506afb42394602fc257b1ad9258d84/examples/nonstandard.rs).
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    /// ```
[581](https://docs.rs#581)    /// # fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    /// # use lexopt::prelude::*;
[583](https://docs.rs#583)    /// # use std::ffi::OsString;
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// # use std::path::PathBuf;
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    /// # let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_iter(&["-13"]);
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// fn parse_dashnum(parser: &mut lexopt::Parser) -> Option<u64> {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    ///     let mut raw = parser.try_raw_args()?;
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    ///     let arg = raw.peek()?.to_str()?;
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    ///     let num = arg.strip_prefix('-')?.parse::<u64>().ok()?;
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    ///     raw.next(); // Consume the argument we just parsed
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    ///     Some(num)
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// }
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    ///
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    /// loop {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    ///     if let Some(num) = parse_dashnum(&mut parser) {
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    ///         println!("Got number {}", num);
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    ///     } else if let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    ///         match arg {
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    ///             // ...
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    ///             # _ => (),
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    ///         }
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    ///     } else {
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    ///         break;
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///     }
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// }
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    /// # Ok(()) }
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    /// ```
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    pub fn try_raw_args(&mut self) -> Option<RawArgs<'_>> {
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        if self.has_pending() {
[610](https://docs.rs#610)            None
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        } else {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)            Some(RawArgs(&mut self.source))
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        }
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// Check whether we're halfway through an argument, or in other words,
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    /// if [`Parser::optional_value()`] would return `Some`.
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    fn has_pending(&self) -> bool {
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        match self.state {
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            State::None | State::FinishedOpts => false,
[621](https://docs.rs#621)            State::PendingValue(_) => true,
[622](https://docs.rs#622)            State::Shorts(ref arg, pos) => pos < arg.len(),
[623](https://docs.rs#623)            #[cfg(windows)]
[624](https://docs.rs#624)            State::ShortsU16(ref arg, pos) => pos < arg.len(),
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        }
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    }
[627](https://docs.rs#627)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    #[inline(never)]
[629](https://docs.rs#629)    fn format_last_option(&self) -> Option<String> {
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        match self.last_option {
[631](https://docs.rs#631)            LastOption::None => None,
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            LastOption::Short(ch) => Some(format!("-{}", ch)),
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            LastOption::Long(ref option) => Some(option.clone()),
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    }
[636](https://docs.rs#636)
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    /// The name of the command, as in the zeroth argument of the process.
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    ///
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    /// This is intended for use in messages. If the name is not valid unicode
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    /// it will be sanitized with replacement characters as by
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// [`String::from_utf8_lossy`].
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    ///
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// To get the current executable, use [`std::env::current_exe`].
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    ///
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// # Example
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    /// ```
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_env();
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    /// let bin_name = parser.bin_name().unwrap_or("myapp");
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    /// println!("{}: Some message", bin_name);
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    /// ```
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    pub fn bin_name(&self) -> Option<&str> {
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        Some(self.bin_name.as_ref()?)
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// Get a value only if it's concatenated to an option, as in `-ovalue` or
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    /// `--option=value` or `-o=value`, but not `-o value` or `--option value`.
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    pub fn optional_value(&mut self) -> Option<OsString> {
[658](https://docs.rs#658)        Some(self.raw_optional_value()?.0)
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    }
[660](https://docs.rs#660)
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// [`Parser::optional_value`], but indicate whether the value was joined
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    /// with an = sign. This matters for [`Parser::values`].
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    fn raw_optional_value(&mut self) -> Option<(OsString, bool)> {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        match replace(&mut self.state, State::None) {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            State::PendingValue(value) => Some((value, true)),
[666](https://docs.rs#666)            State::Shorts(mut arg, mut pos) => {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)                if pos >= arg.len() {
[668](https://docs.rs#668)                    return None;
[669](https://docs.rs#669)                }
[670](https://docs.rs#670)                let mut had_eq_sign = false;
[671](https://docs.rs#671)                if arg[pos] == b'=' && self.short_equals {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)                    // -o=value.
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                    // clap actually strips out all leading '='s, but that seems silly.
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                    // We allow `-xo=value`. Python's argparse doesn't strip the = in that case.
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                    pos += 1;
[676](https://docs.rs#676)                    had_eq_sign = true;
[677](https://docs.rs#677)                }
[678](https://docs.rs#678)                arg.drain(..pos); // Reuse allocation
[679](https://docs.rs#679)                #[cfg(unix)]
[680](https://docs.rs#680)                {
[681](https://docs.rs#681)                    Some((OsString::from_vec(arg), had_eq_sign))
[682](https://docs.rs#682)                }
[683](https://docs.rs#683)                #[cfg(not(unix))]
[684](https://docs.rs#684)                {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)                    let arg = String::from_utf8(arg)
[686](https://docs.rs#686)                        .expect("short option args on exotic platforms must be unicode");
[687](https://docs.rs#687)                    Some((arg.into(), had_eq_sign))
[688](https://docs.rs#688)                }
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            }
[690](https://docs.rs#690)            #[cfg(windows)]
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            State::ShortsU16(arg, mut pos) => {
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                if pos >= arg.len() {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)                    return None;
[694](https://docs.rs#694)                }
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                let mut had_eq_sign = false;
[696](https://docs.rs#696)                if arg[pos] == b'=' as u16 && self.short_equals {
[697](https://docs.rs#697)                    pos += 1;
[698](https://docs.rs#698)                    had_eq_sign = true;
[699](https://docs.rs#699)                }
[700](https://docs.rs#700)                Some((OsString::from_wide(&arg[pos..]), had_eq_sign))
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            }
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            State::FinishedOpts => {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                // Not really supposed to be here, but it's benign and not our fault
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                self.state = State::FinishedOpts;
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                None
[706](https://docs.rs#706)            }
[707](https://docs.rs#707)            State::None => None,
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        }
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    }
[710](https://docs.rs#710)
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    fn new(bin_name: Option<OsString>, source: InnerIter) -> Parser {
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        Parser {
[713](https://docs.rs#713)            source,
[714](https://docs.rs#714)            state: State::None,
[715](https://docs.rs#715)            last_option: LastOption::None,
[716](https://docs.rs#716)            bin_name: bin_name.map(|s| match s.into_string() {
[717](https://docs.rs#717)                Ok(text) => text,
[718](https://docs.rs#718)                Err(text) => text.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
[719](https://docs.rs#719)            }),
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            short_equals: true,
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        }
[722](https://docs.rs#722)    }

[724](https://docs.rs#724)    /// Create a parser from the environment using [`std::env::args_os`].

[727](https://docs.rs#727)    pub fn from_env() -> Parser {
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        let mut source = make_iter(std::env::args_os());
[729](https://docs.rs#729)        Parser::new(source.next(), source)

[732](https://docs.rs#732)    // The collision with `FromIterator::from_iter` is a bit unfortunate.
[733](https://docs.rs#733)    // This name is used because:
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    // - `from_args()` was taken, and changing its behavior without changing
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    //   its signature would be evil.
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    // - structopt also had a method by that name, so there's a precedent.
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    //   (clap_derive doesn't.)
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    // - I couldn't think of a better one.
[739](https://docs.rs#739)    // When this name was chosen `FromIterator` could not actually be implemented.
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    // It can be implemented now, but I'm not sure there's a reason to.

[742](https://docs.rs#742)    /// Create a parser from an iterator. This is useful for testing among other things.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    ///
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    /// The first item from the iterator **must** be the binary name, as from [`std::env::args_os`].
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    ///
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    /// The iterator is consumed immediately.
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    ///
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    /// # Example
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    /// ```
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    /// let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_iter(&["myapp", "-n", "10", "./foo.bar"]);
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    /// ```
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    pub fn from_iter<I>(args: I) -> Parser
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    where
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        I: IntoIterator,
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        I::Item: Into<OsString>,
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    {
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        let mut args = make_iter(args.into_iter().map(Into::into));
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        Parser::new(args.next(), args)
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    }
[760](https://docs.rs#760)
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    /// Create a parser from an iterator that does **not** include the binary name.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    ///

[764](https://docs.rs#764)    ///

[767](https://docs.rs#767)    pub fn from_args<I>(args: I) -> Parser

[773](https://docs.rs#773)    }

[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// Store a long option so the caller can borrow it.
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    fn set_long(&mut self, option: String) -> Arg<'_> {

[778](https://docs.rs#778)        match self.last_option {
[779](https://docs.rs#779)            LastOption::Long(ref option) => Arg::Long(&option[2..]),
[780](https://docs.rs#780)            _ => unreachable!(),

[783](https://docs.rs#783)
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    /// Configure whether to parse an equals sign (`=`) for short options.
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    ///
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    /// If this is **true** (the default), `-o=foobar` will be interpreted as
[787](https://docs.rs#787)    /// the option `-o` with the value `foobar`.
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    ///
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    /// If this is **false**, `-o=foobar` will be interpreted as
[790](https://docs.rs#790)    /// the option `-o` with the value `=foobar`.
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    ///
[792](https://docs.rs#792)    /// Note that even if this is `true` the equals sign is optional. That is,
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// `-ofoobar` and `-o foobar` are always interpreted as `-o` with the value
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// `foobar` regardless of this setting.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    ///
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// Most other argument parsers treat the equals sign as part of the value,
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    /// but the syntax is notably accepted by [`clap`](https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/)
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// and by Python's [`argparse`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html).
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    ///
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// You may want to disable this setting if it's common for an option's value
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    /// to start with an equals sign. The Unix `cut` command for example is sometimes
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// used with `-d=`, where `"="` is the value belonging to the `-d` option. By default
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    /// the empty string `""` is parsed instead.
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    ///
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    /// # Example
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    ///
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// You can configure this right after creating the parser:
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// ```
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    /// let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_env();
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// parser.set_short_equals(false);
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// ```
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    ///
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    /// You could also do it temporarily, for an individual option:
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    /// ```
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// # fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// # use lexopt::prelude::*;
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    /// # let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_args(&["-d=", "key=value"]);
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    /// # let mut delimiter = None;
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    /// # while let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    /// # match arg {
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// Short('d') | Long("delimiter") => {
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    ///     parser.set_short_equals(false);
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    ///     delimiter = Some(parser.value()?.string()?);
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    ///     parser.set_short_equals(true);
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// }
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    /// # _ => (), }} Ok(()) }
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    /// ```
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    pub fn set_short_equals(&mut self, on: bool) {
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        self.short_equals = on;
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    }
[831](https://docs.rs#831)}

[838](https://docs.rs#838)            Arg::Long(long) => Error::UnexpectedOption(format!("--{}", long)),
[839](https://docs.rs#839)            Arg::Value(value) => Error::UnexpectedArgument(value),
[840](https://docs.rs#840)        }
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    }

[844](https://docs.rs#844)/// An iterator for multiple option-arguments, returned by [`Parser::values`].
[845](https://docs.rs#845)///
[846](https://docs.rs#846)/// It's guaranteed to yield at least one value.
[847](https://docs.rs#847)#[derive(Debug)]
[848](https://docs.rs#848)pub struct ValuesIter<'a> {
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    took_first: bool,
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    parser: Option<&'a mut Parser>,
[851](https://docs.rs#851)}
[852](https://docs.rs#852)
[853](https://docs.rs#853)impl Iterator for ValuesIter<'_> {
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    type Item = OsString;
[855](https://docs.rs#855)
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
[857](https://docs.rs#857)        let parser = self.parser.as_mut()?;
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        if self.took_first {
[859](https://docs.rs#859)            parser.next_if_normal()
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        } else if let Some((value, had_eq_sign)) = parser.raw_optional_value() {
[861](https://docs.rs#861)            if had_eq_sign {
[862](https://docs.rs#862)                self.parser = None;
[863](https://docs.rs#863)            }
[864](https://docs.rs#864)            self.took_first = true;
[865](https://docs.rs#865)            Some(value)
[866](https://docs.rs#866)        } else {
[867](https://docs.rs#867)            let value = parser
[868](https://docs.rs#868)                .next_if_normal()
[869](https://docs.rs#869)                .expect("ValuesIter must yield at least one value");
[870](https://docs.rs#870)            self.took_first = true;
[871](https://docs.rs#871)            Some(value)
[872](https://docs.rs#872)        }
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    }

[925](https://docs.rs#925)/// An error during argument parsing.
[926](https://docs.rs#926)///
[927](https://docs.rs#927)/// This implements `From<String>` and `From<&str>`, for easy ad-hoc error
[928](https://docs.rs#928)/// messages.
[929](https://docs.rs#929)//
[930](https://docs.rs#930)// This is not #[non_exhaustive] because of the MSRV. I'm hoping no more
[931](https://docs.rs#931)// variants will turn out to be needed: this seems reasonable, if the scope
[932](https://docs.rs#932)// of the library doesn't change. Worst case scenario it can be stuffed inside
[933](https://docs.rs#933)// Error::Custom.
[934](https://docs.rs#934)pub enum Error {
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// An option argument was expected but was not found.
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    MissingValue {
[937](https://docs.rs#937)        /// The most recently emitted option.
[938](https://docs.rs#938)        option: Option<String>,
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    },
[940](https://docs.rs#940)
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    /// An unexpected option was found.
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    UnexpectedOption(String),
[943](https://docs.rs#943)
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    /// A positional argument was found when none was expected.
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    UnexpectedArgument(OsString),
[946](https://docs.rs#946)
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    /// An option had a value when none was expected.
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    UnexpectedValue {
[949](https://docs.rs#949)        /// The option.
[950](https://docs.rs#950)        option: String,
[951](https://docs.rs#951)        /// The value.
[952](https://docs.rs#952)        value: OsString,
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    },
[954](https://docs.rs#954)
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    /// Parsing a value failed. Returned by methods on [`ValueExt`].
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    ParsingFailed {
[957](https://docs.rs#957)        /// The string that failed to parse.
[958](https://docs.rs#958)        value: String,
[959](https://docs.rs#959)        /// The error returned while parsing.
[960](https://docs.rs#960)        error: Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>,
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    },
[962](https://docs.rs#962)
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// A value was found that was not valid unicode.
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    ///
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// This can be returned by the methods on [`ValueExt`].
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    NonUnicodeValue(OsString),
[967](https://docs.rs#967)
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// For custom error messages in application code.
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    Custom(Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>),
[970](https://docs.rs#970)}

[972](https://docs.rs#972)impl Display for Error {
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[974](https://docs.rs#974)        use crate::Error::*;
[975](https://docs.rs#975)        match self {
[976](https://docs.rs#976)            MissingValue { option: None } => write!(f, "missing argument"),
[977](https://docs.rs#977)            MissingValue {
[978](https://docs.rs#978)                option: Some(option),
[979](https://docs.rs#979)            } => {
[980](https://docs.rs#980)                write!(f, "missing argument for option '{}'", option)
[981](https://docs.rs#981)            }
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            UnexpectedOption(option) => write!(f, "invalid option '{}'", option),
[983](https://docs.rs#983)            UnexpectedArgument(value) => write!(f, "unexpected argument {:?}", value),
[984](https://docs.rs#984)            UnexpectedValue { option, value } => {
[985](https://docs.rs#985)                write!(
[986](https://docs.rs#986)                    f,
[987](https://docs.rs#987)                    "unexpected argument for option '{}': {:?}",
[988](https://docs.rs#988)                    option, value
[989](https://docs.rs#989)                )
[990](https://docs.rs#990)            }
[991](https://docs.rs#991)            NonUnicodeValue(value) => write!(f, "argument is invalid unicode: {:?}", value),
[992](https://docs.rs#992)            ParsingFailed { value, error } => {
[993](https://docs.rs#993)                write!(f, "cannot parse argument {:?}: {}", value, error)
[994](https://docs.rs#994)            }
[995](https://docs.rs#995)            Custom(err) => write!(f, "{}", err),
[996](https://docs.rs#996)        }
[997](https://docs.rs#997)    }

[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)/// For [`OsString::into_string`], so it may be used with the try (`?`) operator.
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)///
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)/// [`ValueExt::string`] is the new preferred method because it's compatible with
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)/// catch-all error types like `anyhow::Error`.
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)impl From<OsString> for Error {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)    fn from(arg: OsString) -> Self {
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)        Error::NonUnicodeValue(arg)
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)    }
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)}
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)mod private {
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)    pub trait Sealed {}
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)    impl Sealed for std::ffi::OsString {}
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)}
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)/// An optional extension trait with methods for parsing [`OsString`]s.
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)///
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)/// They may fail in two cases:
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)/// - The value cannot be decoded because it's invalid unicode
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)///   ([`Error::NonUnicodeValue`])
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)/// - The value can be decoded, but parsing fails ([`Error::ParsingFailed`])
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)///
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)/// If parsing fails the error will be wrapped in lexopt's own [`Error`] type.
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)pub trait ValueExt: private::Sealed {
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)    /// Decode the value and parse it using [`FromStr`].
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    ///
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)    /// This will fail if the value is not valid unicode or if the subsequent
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)    /// parsing fails.
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)    fn parse<T: FromStr>(&self) -> Result<T, Error>
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    where
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)        T::Err: Into<Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>>;
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)    // TODO: move the F parameter to the end for better turbofishing.
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)    // This is a breaking change that affects at least one real-world program.
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)    // But the code will be better off for it, so it's worth doing in the next
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)    // breaking release.
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)    /// Decode the value and parse it using a custom function.
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)    fn parse_with<F, T, E>(&self, func: F) -> Result<T, Error>
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)    where
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)        F: FnOnce(&str) -> Result<T, E>,
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)        E: Into<Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>>;
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)    // There is no parse_os_with() because I can't think of any useful
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    // fallible operations on an OsString. Typically you'd either decode it,
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)    // use it as is, or do an infallible conversion to a PathBuf or such.
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)    //
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)    // If you have a use for parse_os_with() please open an issue with an
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)    // example.
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)    /// Convert the `OsString` into a [`String`] if it's valid Unicode.
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)    ///
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)    /// This is like [`OsString::into_string`] but returns an
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)    /// [`Error::NonUnicodeValue`] on error instead of the original `OsString`.
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)    /// This makes it easier to propagate the failure with libraries like
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)    /// `anyhow`.
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)    fn string(self) -> Result<String, Error>;
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)}
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)impl ValueExt for OsString {
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)    fn parse<T: FromStr>(&self) -> Result<T, Error>
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)    where
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)        T::Err: Into<Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>>,
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)    {
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)        self.parse_with(FromStr::from_str)
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)    }
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)    fn parse_with<F, T, E>(&self, func: F) -> Result<T, Error>
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)    where
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        F: FnOnce(&str) -> Result<T, E>,
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)        E: Into<Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static>>,
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)    {
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)        match self.to_str() {
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)            Some(text) => match func(text) {
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)                Ok(value) => Ok(value),
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)                Err(err) => Err(Error::ParsingFailed {
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)                    value: text.to_owned(),
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)                    error: err.into(),
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)                }),
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            },
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)            None => Err(Error::NonUnicodeValue(self.into())),
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        }
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)    }
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)    fn string(self) -> Result<String, Error> {
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)        match self.into_string() {
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)            Ok(string) => Ok(string),
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)            Err(raw) => Err(Error::NonUnicodeValue(raw)),
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)        }
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)    }
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)}
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)/// A small prelude for processing arguments.
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)///
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)/// It allows you to write `Short`/`Long`/`Value` without an [`Arg`] prefix
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)/// and adds convenience methods to [`OsString`].
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)///
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)/// If this is used it's best to import it inside a function, not in module
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)/// scope:
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)/// ```
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)/// # struct Args;
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)/// fn parse_args() -> Result<Args, lexopt::Error> {
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)///     use lexopt::prelude::*;
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)///     // ...
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)///     # Ok(Args)
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)/// }
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)/// ```
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)pub mod prelude {
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    pub use super::Arg::*;
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    pub use super::ValueExt;
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)}
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)/// Take the first codepoint from a UTF-8 bytestring.
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)///
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)/// The rest of the bytestring does not have to be valid unicode.
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)fn first_codepoint(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<char>, Utf8Error> {
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    // We only need the first 4 bytes
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    let bytes = bytes.get(..4).unwrap_or(bytes);
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    let text = match std::str::from_utf8(bytes) {
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)        Ok(text) => text,
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)        Err(err) if err.valid_up_to() > 0 => {
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)            std::str::from_utf8(&bytes[..err.valid_up_to()]).unwrap()
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        }
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        Err(err) => return Err(err),
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)    };
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)    Ok(text.chars().next())
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)}
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)#[cfg(windows)]
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)/// As before, but for UTF-16.
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)fn first_utf16_codepoint(units: &[u16]) -> Result<Option<char>, u16> {
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)    match std::char::decode_utf16(units.iter().cloned()).next() {
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)        Some(Ok(ch)) => Ok(Some(ch)),
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)        Some(Err(_)) => Err(units[0]),
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)        None => Ok(None),
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)    }
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)}

[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    /// Transform @ characters into invalid unicode.
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)    fn bad_string(text: &str) -> OsString {
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)        #[cfg(any(unix, all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1")))]
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)        {
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)            let mut text = text.as_bytes().to_vec();
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)            for ch in &mut text {
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)                if *ch == b'@' {
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)                    *ch = b'\xFF';
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)                }
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)            }
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)            OsString::from_vec(text)
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)        }
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)        #[cfg(windows)]
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)        {
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)            let mut out = Vec::new();
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)            for ch in text.chars() {
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)                if ch == '@' {
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)                    out.push(0xD800);
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)                } else {
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)                    let mut buf = [0; 2];
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)                    out.extend(&*ch.encode_utf16(&mut buf));
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)                }
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)            }
[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)            OsString::from_wide(&out)
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)        }
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)        #[cfg(not(any(unix, windows, all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1"))))]
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)        {
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)            if text.contains('@') {
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)                unimplemented!("Don't know how to create invalid OsStrings on this platform");
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)            }
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)            text.into()
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)        }
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)    }
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)    /// [`bad_string`] for text that has been processed.
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)    ///
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)    /// On wasip1 we test invalid OS strings but the crate doesn't preserve them.
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)    ///
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)    /// On other targets this is identical to `bad_string`.
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)    #[allow(unused)]
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)    fn bad_output_string(text: &str) -> OsString {
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)        #[cfg(all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1"))]
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)        return text.replace("@", "�").into();
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)        #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1")))]
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)        return bad_string(text);
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)    }
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)    /// Basic exhaustive testing of short combinations of "interesting"
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)    /// arguments. They should not panic, not hang, and pass some checks.
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)    ///
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)    /// The advantage compared to full fuzzing is that it runs on all platforms
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    /// and together with the other tests. cargo-fuzz doesn't work on Windows
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)    /// and requires a special incantation.
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    ///
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// A disadvantage is that it's still limited by arguments I could think of
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// and only does very short sequences. Another is that it's bad at
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    /// reporting failure, though the println!() helps.
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    ///
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    /// This test takes a while to run.
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    #[test]
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    fn basic_fuzz() {
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)        #[cfg(any(windows, unix, all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1")))]
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)        const VOCABULARY: &[&str] = &[
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)            "", "-", "--", "---", "a", "-a", "-aa", "@", "-@", "-a@", "-@a", "--a", "--@", "--a=a",
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)            "--a=", "--a=@", "--@=a", "--=", "--=@", "--=a", "-@@", "-a=a", "-a=", "-=", "-a-",
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)        ];
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)        #[cfg(not(any(windows, unix, all(target_os = "wasi", target_env = "p1"))))]
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)        const VOCABULARY: &[&str] = &[
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)            "", "-", "--", "---", "a", "-a", "-aa", "--a", "--a=a", "--a=", "--=", "--=a", "-a=a",
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)            "-a=", "-=", "-a-",
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)        ];
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)        exhaust(Parser::new(None, Vec::new().into_iter()), 0);
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)        let vocabulary: Vec<OsString> = VOCABULARY.iter().map(|&s| bad_string(s)).collect();
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)        let mut permutations = vec![vec![]];
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)        for _ in 0..3 {
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)            let mut new = Vec::new();
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)            for old in permutations {
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)                for word in &vocabulary {
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)                    let mut extended = old.clone();
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)                    extended.push(word);
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)                    new.push(extended);
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)                }
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)            }
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)            permutations = new;
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)            for permutation in &permutations {
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)                println!("{:?}", permutation);
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)                let p = Parser::from_args(permutation);
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)                exhaust(p, 0);
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)            }
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)        }
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)    }
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)    /// Run many sequences of methods on a Parser.
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)    fn exhaust(mut parser: Parser, depth: u16) {
[1983](https://docs.rs#1983)        if depth > 100 {
[1984](https://docs.rs#1984)            panic!("Stuck in loop");
[1985](https://docs.rs#1985)        }
[1986](https://docs.rs#1986)
[1987](https://docs.rs#1987)        // has_pending() == optional_value().is_some()
[1988](https://docs.rs#1988)        if parser.has_pending() {
[1989](https://docs.rs#1989)            {
[1990](https://docs.rs#1990)                let mut parser = parser.clone();
[1991](https://docs.rs#1991)                assert!(parser.try_raw_args().is_none());
[1992](https://docs.rs#1992)                assert!(parser.try_raw_args().is_none());
[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)                assert!(parser.raw_args().is_err());
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)                // Recovery possible
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)                assert!(parser.raw_args().is_ok());
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)                assert!(parser.try_raw_args().is_some());
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)            }
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)            {
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)                let mut parser = parser.clone();

# Parser in lexopt - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/lexopt/latest/target-redirect/lexopt/struct.Parser.html

`pub struct Parser { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A parser for command line arguments.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get the next option or positional argument.

A return value of `Ok(None)` means the command line has been exhausted.

Options that are not valid unicode are transformed with replacement
characters as by [ String::from_utf8_lossy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.from_utf8_lossy).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

[ Error::UnexpectedValue](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.UnexpectedValue) is returned if the last option had a
value that hasn’t been consumed, as in

`--option=value` or `-o=value`.It’s possible to continue parsing after an error (but this is rarely useful).

```
17fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
18    use lexopt::prelude::*;
19
20    let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_env();
21    parser.set_short_equals(false);
22    let mut free = Vec::new();
23    while let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
24        match arg {
25            Short('n') | Long("number") => {
26                let num: u16 = parser.value()?.parse()?;
27                println!("Got number {}", num);
28            }
29            Long("shout") => {
30                println!("Got --shout");
31            }
32            Value(val) => {
33                free.push(val);
34                free.extend(parser.raw_args()?);
35            }
36            _ => return Err(arg.unexpected()),
37        }
38    }
39    println!("Got free args {:?}", free);
40    Ok(())
41}

9fn main() -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
10    use lexopt::prelude::*;
11
12    let mut settings = GlobalSettings {
13        toolchain: "stable".to_owned(),
14        color: Color::Auto,
15        offline: false,
16        quiet: false,
17        verbose: false,
18    };
19
20    let mut parser = lexopt::Parser::from_env();
21    while let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
22        match arg {
23            Long("color") => {
24                settings.color = parser.value()?.parse()?;
25            }
26            Long("offline") => {
27                settings.offline = true;
28            }
29            Long("quiet") => {
30                settings.quiet = true;
31                settings.verbose = false;
32            }
33            Long("verbose") => {
34                settings.verbose = true;
35                settings.quiet = false;
36            }
37            Long("help") => {
38                println!("{}", HELP);
39                std::process::exit(0);
40            }
41            Value(value) => {
42                let value = value.string()?;
43                match value.as_str() {
44                    value if value.starts_with('+') => {
45                        settings.toolchain = value[1..].to_owned();
46                    }
47                    "install" => {
48                        return install(settings, parser);
49                    }
50                    value => {
51                        return Err(format!("unknown subcommand '{}'", value).into());
52                    }
53                }
54            }
55            _ => return Err(arg.unexpected()),
56        }
57    }
58
59    println!("{}", HELP);
60    Ok(())
61}

72fn install(settings: GlobalSettings, mut parser: lexopt::Parser) -> Result<(), lexopt::Error> {
73    use lexopt::prelude::*;
74
75    let mut package: Option<String> = None;
76    let mut root: Option<PathBuf> = None;
77    let mut jobs: u16 = get_no_of_cpus();
78
79    while let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
80        match arg {
81            Value(value) if package.is_none() => {
82                package = Some(value.string()?);
83            }
84            Long("root") => {
85                root = Some(parser.value()?.into());
86            }
87            Short('j') | Long("jobs") => {
88                jobs = parser.value()?.parse()?;
89            }
90            Long("help") => {
91                println!("cargo install [OPTIONS] CRATE");
92                std::process::exit(0);
93            }
94            _ => return Err(arg.unexpected()),
95        }
96    }
97
98    println!("Settings: {:#?}", settings);
99    println!(
100        "Installing {} into {:?} with {} jobs",
101        package.ok_or("missing CRATE argument")?,
102        root,
103        jobs
104    );
105
106    Ok(())
107}

Get a value for an option.

This function should normally be called right after seeing an option
that expects a value, with positional arguments being collected
using [ next()](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.next).

A value is collected even if it looks like an option
(i.e., starts with `-`).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

An [ Error::MissingValue](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.MissingValue) is returned if the end of the command
line is reached.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lexopt/lib.rs.html#459-475)#### pub fn [values](https://docs.rs#method.values)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[ValuesIter](https://docs.rs/struct.ValuesIter.html)<'_>, [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lexopt/lib.rs.html#459-475)

#### pub fn [values](https://docs.rs#method.values)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[ValuesIter](https://docs.rs/struct.ValuesIter.html)<'_>, [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Gather multiple values for an option.

This is used for options that take multiple arguments, such as a
`--command` flag that’s invoked as `app --command echo 'Hello world'`.

It will gather arguments until another option is found, or `--` is found, or
the end of the command line is reached. This differs from `.value()`, which
takes a value even if it looks like an option.

On success the resulting iterator will yield at least one value.

An equals sign (`=`) will limit this to a single value. That means `-a=b c` and
`--opt=b c` will only yield `"b"` while `-a b c`, `-ab c` and `--opt b c` will
yield `"b"`, `"c"`.

(If [ short_equals](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.set_short_equals) is disabled then

`-a=b c` will yield
`"=b"`, `"c"`.)[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

If not at least one value is found then [ Error::MissingValue](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.MissingValue) is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let arguments: Vec<OsString> = parser.values()?.collect();
let at_most_three_files: Vec<PathBuf> = parser.values()?.take(3).map(Into::into).collect();
for value in parser.values()? {
    // ...
}
```
Take raw arguments from the original command line.

This returns an iterator of [ OsString](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsString.html)s. Any arguments that are not
consumed are kept, so you can continue parsing after you’re done with
the iterator.

To inspect an argument without consuming it, use [ RawArgs::peek](https://docs.rs/struct.RawArgs.html#method.peek) or

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.RawArgs.html#method.as_slice)

`RawArgs::as_slice`[§](https://docs.rs#errors-3)Errors

Returns an [ Error::UnexpectedValue](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.UnexpectedValue) if the last option had a left-over
argument, as in

`--option=value`, `-ovalue`, or if it was midway through
an option chain, as in `-abc`. The iterator only yields whole arguments.
To avoid this, use [.](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.try_raw_args)

`try_raw_args()`After this error the method is guaranteed to succeed, as it consumes the rest of the argument.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

As soon as a free-standing argument is found, consume the other arguments as-is, and build them into a command.

```
Value(prog) => {
    let args: Vec<_> = parser.raw_args()?.collect();
    let command = std::process::Command::new(prog).args(args);
}

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lexopt/lib.rs.html#608-614)#### pub fn [try_raw_args](https://docs.rs#method.try_raw_args)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[RawArgs](https://docs.rs/struct.RawArgs.html)<'_>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/lexopt/lib.rs.html#608-614)

#### pub fn [try_raw_args](https://docs.rs#method.try_raw_args)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[RawArgs](https://docs.rs/struct.RawArgs.html)<'_>>

Take raw arguments from the original command line, *if* the current argument
has finished processing.

Unlike [ raw_args()](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.raw_args) this does not consume any value
in case of a left-over argument. This makes it safe to call at any time.

It returns `None` exactly when [ optional_value()](https://docs.rs/struct.Parser.html#method.optional_value)
would return

`Some`.Note: If no arguments are left then it returns an empty iterator (not `None`).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

Process arguments of the form `-123` as numbers. For a complete runnable version of
this example, see
[ examples/nonstandard.rs](https://github.com/blyxxyz/lexopt/blob/e3754e6f24506afb42394602fc257b1ad9258d84/examples/nonstandard.rs).

```
fn parse_dashnum(parser: &mut lexopt::Parser) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut raw = parser.try_raw_args()?;
    let arg = raw.peek()?.to_str()?;
    let num = arg.strip_prefix('-')?.parse::<u64>().ok()?;
    raw.next(); // Consume the argument we just parsed
    Some(num)
}
loop {
    if let Some(num) = parse_dashnum(&mut parser) {
        println!("Got number {}", num);
    } else if let Some(arg) = parser.next()? {
        match arg {
            // ...
        }
    } else {
        break;
    }
}
```
The name of the command, as in the zeroth argument of the process.

This is intended for use in messages. If the name is not valid unicode
it will be sanitized with replacement characters as by
[ String::from_utf8_lossy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.from_utf8_lossy).

To get the current executable, use [ std::env::current_exe](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.current_exe.html).

println!("{}: Some message", bin_name);
